title: Noetherian cartesian model of a finitely presented affine morphism
statement: Let $R\to B$ be a finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. There exist commutative rings $R_0,B_0$, homomorphisms $R_0\to B_0$, $R_0\to R$, $B_0\to B$ forming a commutative square, and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $B_0\otimes_{R_0}R\cong B$ sending $b\otimes r$ to the product of their images. The ring $R_0$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and $B_0$ is of finite type over $R_0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]; both rings are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Writing $h:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $h_0:\operatorname{Spec}B_0\to\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ for the induced morphisms [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the displayed isomorphism identifies $h$ with the base change of $h_0$ along $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with other projection $q:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ induced by $B_0\to B$. The morphism $h_0$ is locally of finite type, $q$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme].

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation $B\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ using [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $C\subseteq R$ be the union of the coefficient sets of the finitely many $f_j$. Each polynomial has finite support by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], so $C$ is finite. Define $R_0$ to be the image in $R$ of the evaluation map $\mathbf Z[t_c:c\in C]\to R$, $t_c\mapsto c$. Thus $R_0$ is a subring of $R$ generated over $\mathbf Z$ by the finite set $C$, hence of finite type by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Regard each $f_j$ as a polynomial $f_{j,0}$ over $R_0$, and set $B_0=R_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_{1,0},\ldots,f_{m,0})$. Its variable classes generate it as an $R_0$-algebra. Coefficient inclusion and the chosen presentation induce $B_0\to B$; this and $R_0\hookrightarrow R$ form the required commutative square.

source.place: Tag 00QJ (lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-quasi-compact-open-upstairs), proof: choose the finite coefficient subalgebra and the quotient by the same relations

proof.text: The ring $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian: a nonzero ideal contains a least positive integer $d$, and division by $d$ shows that every element of the ideal is a multiple of $d$; the zero ideal is generated by $0$. Thus every ideal is finitely generated, as required by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] first to $\mathbf Z\to R_0$, and then to $R_0\to B_0$, using the two finite-type assertions just proved. This proves that both $R_0$ and $B_0$ are Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), applied to the finite-coefficient model in the proof of Tag 00QJ

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] to the quotient presentation of $B_0$ over $R_0$ and the map $R_0\hookrightarrow R$. Its hypotheses hold because the quotient map from $R_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ is surjective with kernel generated by the $f_{j,0}$; their coefficient images are exactly $f_j$. It gives $B_0\otimes_{R_0}R\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\cong B$. The isomorphism sends $\bar x_i\otimes1$ to the chosen generator of $B$ and $1\otimes r$ to the image of $r$. Consequently it is the canonical map $b\otimes r\mapsto\beta(b)\varphi(r)$: these maps agree on $R$ and on the variable classes, which generate $B_0$ over $R_0$. This checks the requested normalization, as well as invertibility.

source.place: Tag 00QJ, proof: S = R tensor over R_0 S_0; Section Tag 05G3 (section-base-change), presentation formula after Definition 05G4

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $\operatorname{Spec}B_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R_0}\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B_0\otimes_{R_0}R)$, with projections induced by $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ and $r\mapsto1\otimes r$. Take the spectrum of the inverse of the preceding algebra isomorphism to identify this scheme with $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Functoriality of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the two generator formulas identify its projections with $q=\operatorname{Spec}(B_0\to B)$ and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(R\to B)$ respectively. Thus the commutative square of spectra is cartesian, with exactly the maps claimed.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), affine fibre product formula and its universal-property proof

proof.text: For $h_0$, take the entire source $\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ and target $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ as the affine neighbourhoods of every source point. Their section-ring map is $R_0\to B_0$, which is finite type; [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion] therefore proves that $h_0$ is locally of finite type. Both endpoints of $q$ are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] makes $q$ affine, and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes it quasi-compact. Finally $\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ has the one-member affine cover consisting of itself, whose section ring is the Noetherian ring $B_0$; it is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs].
